conventions.convention: The fixed likelihood section is measurable and nonnegative, possibly infinite. The evidence lies in [0,+∞]; the quotient update is defined only when the evidence is finite and strictly positive.

A proper prior has total mass one; an improper prior here is sigma-finite with infinite total mass. An improper-prior fiberwise normalizer does not itself supply a prior-predictive probability or conditional law.
Separate pointwise likelihood sections do not imply joint parameter-data measurability; the latter must be supplied for Tonelli-based prior-predictive arguments.
The normalization proposition permits an arbitrary measure space, without sigma-finiteness, and only finite strictly positive scaling constants c.

The normal example assumes AC, n≥1, and known variance σ²>0. The parameter sigma-algebra is the Lebesgue sigma-algebra; the data sigma-algebra and measure are recursive finite products. Identification with N(ȳ,σ²/n) is explicitly restricted to Borel sets.

The Beta(0,0) prior is a measure on the open interval (0,1), with restricted Lebesgue sigma-algebra and density 1/[p(1−p)]. The endpoint observations are y=0 and y=n for n≥1; AC supplies countable choice for the cited Lebesgue results.

At the finite model's predictive-null datum 2, the likelihood quotient is undefined; the dominated Bayes theorem's specified value is the prior filler, which is a conditional-version value rather than an observation-determined update.

load_bearing.statement: For a sigma-finite prior measure Π and a fixed nonnegative measurable likelihood section L_y, define Z_Π(y)=∫L_y dΠ. Only when 0<Z_Π(y)<+∞ define Π_y(A)=∫_A L_y dΠ/Z_Π(y).

Let (Θ,T,Π) be a measure space, let L_y:Θ→[0,+∞] be measurable for a fixed datum y, and put Z=∫_Θ L_y dΠ. For a finite positive constant c, A↦c∫_A L_y dΠ is a probability measure if and only if 0<Z<+∞ and c=Z⁻¹.

seams_checked.note: The proper-prior and sampling-kernel conventions agree. Both pages distinguish a fixed-fiber update, a sample-point posterior RCD, and a data-indexed conditional kernel; the reverse reference places fiberwise propriety on the next page without asserting additional existence.

The conjugate updates use finite positive evidence for normalization and separately invoke the dominated-kernel theorem for conditional-law identification. Endpoint counts and zero-exposure exclusions preserve the supplier's normalization domain.

The page and predictive definition require a supplied measurable probability kernel. Their dominated construction explicitly retains proper prior, sigma-finite data measure, joint density measurability, and version-dependent null-data values.

Marginal evidence specializes the fixed-fiber definition to proper model priors. Model odds and empirical-Bayes updates impose finite positive evidence; predictive-density interpretation additionally retains jointly measurable normalized sampling densities and a common sigma-finite data measure.

The consistency theorem supplies a proper prior and jointly measurable normalized dominated density, defines the quotient only on finite-positive fibers, and uses the prior filler elsewhere. It does not infer joint measurability from separate likelihood versions.

The loss update uses the same finite-positive normalization regime and proves probability normalization independently. Its page expressly requires additional sampling-model hypotheses before claiming a conditional-law interpretation.

The latent-density definition and marginal theorem require a supplied jointly measurable density and sigma-finite reference measures. Pointwise conditional densities are restricted to positive finite marginal fibers, consistently with the supplier's warning and normalization domain.

The recursive filter uses a predictive probability as the prior, supplied jointly measurable normalized observation densities, and sigma-finite reference measures. Its theorem applies the dominated Bayes formula at each fixed history and retains predictive-law fillers at zero or infinite evidence.
